doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: No gigs: musicians and the pandemic
summary: Stripling jokes about always saying 'I can do it' when the phone rings; now nobody calls. He reflects on making people happy and on clubs and rents hit by Covid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Just before I hit the record button we were talking about, I’m just looking for a gig. Do you want to expand on that?

Well it goes to the pandemic and Covid actually. Musicians always joke about that, and you know, the question is when the phone rings, the joke is when the phone rings I just pick up the phone and say, “I can do it.” You know? And that’s the thing. That’s the joke. And we don’t do that, because there’s a lot of parameters that you want for any time that you work. But the unfortunate part of where we’re at in terms on being in Covid-19 and dealing with this is that nobody is gonna call you. And that can be tragic for a musician because the one thing that you can do, you can’t do it. And I smile out of my pain, but the one thing that — I can play for people. I can sing for them, I can make people happy. I mean I honestly feel kind of like we’re put here as musicians to make people happy. I feel that the theater is a magical place, a place where people can go and — remember that old song “Forget your troubles, come on get happy” right? That’s what music does for people. It’s a chance for people to go into the theater and get that experience. And I and my friends, that’s what we do. And now we’re placed in a situation where we can’t do what we do because people will die if we do it, you know, if they come together. And so that’s just been a difficult thing to grasp, I mean imagine having two kids in college and you can’t do what you can do. And then, you know, you look at the inequities of some people do great during a pandemic. If you’re Amazon, you know, great. You can deliver stuff right to their house you know? I can’t do that. You know if you’re a grocery store you can raise your prices if you want to because you know that people have to come to you. They might even want it delivered, but in any case, they’re going to the grocery

store. If you’re a restaurant that’s not going to happen. If you’re Small’s in New York City — I mean I live in Columbus, Ohio, but I’m reading about what’s happening to the clubs, Small’s, Mezzro is another one, and the rent people are like, “We don’t care if you can’t have people in the nightclub. Where’s my money?” So these are unfortunate circumstances.
